findings.passage: The fact remains, voter ID laws do not discriminate or disenfranchise; they ensure integrity at the ballot box.
findings.note: Statement issued in his name after the federal court upheld South Carolina's 2011 photo ID law (South Carolina v. United States). He also said the ruling affirms the law is valid under the Voting Rights Act and that his office will work to implement it.

findings.passage: I believe voter ID laws are important to ensure the integrity and confidence of our elections.

findings.passage: I've defended election integrity time and time again and even sued the federal government when the Obama administration tried to outlaw our voter ID laws here in South Carolina.

findings.passage: “This couldn’t be simpler. The upcoming election needs to be fair and honest, and this act would ensure that only U.S. citizens vote in federal elections,” Attorney General Wilson said.

findings.passage: “This would seem like common sense. If only citizens can vote, what’s wrong with requiring proof of citizenship to register to vote?” asks Attorney General Wilson.

The states are required by law to protect our election process and are trying to do that, and the Department of Homeland Security is required by law to verify voter information upon request, but DHS has either delayed or given us inadequate information,” Attorney General Wilson said.
findings.note: Quote in a release about a 16-state letter he co-led asking the federal homeland security department to verify the immigration status of registered voters on request.

findings.passage: Requiring proof of citizenship is just common sense; it protects our democracy and restores public trust.

findings.passage: “We want to protect the integrity of everyone’s ballots, including people who vote by mail, and it’s our position that counting mail-in ballots that come in after Election Day opens up the system to fraud,” Attorney General Wilson said.
